title_original: Amid a Historic Downturn, Art Basel Miami Beach Threatened to Move to Las Vegas
excerpt_original: MCH, the fair’s parent group, once faced insolvency and is now seeing a once-in-a-generation downturn.

blocks.text: Miami Beach , once an outback on the map of the international art world, is now able to make an argument for itself as a cultural hub. A major player in that trajectory, if not the sole cause, is the Art Basel Miami Beach fair, which held its first edition in the Florida city in 2002.

But a New York Times report goes inside a sharp-elbowed fight over the future location of the fair, whose executives demanded that the city cut in half the rent it pays on the Miami Beach Convention Center, where the fair takes place annually in early December. The fair had been paying about $1 million a year for the gigantic space, which has hosted nearly 300 galleries in some editions. The center features a 60,000-square-foot ballroom and 1.4 million square feet of flexible exhibition space, according to marketing materials. It underwent a $640 million renovation and expansion between 2015 and 2020.

Art Basel has had a direct impact of $60 million on the city and annually draws some 80,000 visitors. Launched by dealers in Switzerland in 1970, Basel expanded to Miami Beach in 2002, Hong Kong in 2013, Paris in 2022, and Qatar in 2026. The fair did not immediately respond to a request for comment, sent to its press representative.

City commissioner David Suarez, per the Times , asked, “If this deal doesn’t move forward, is Art Basel ready to walk from Miami Beach?” Art Basel chief executive Noah Horowitz said that in the absence of a rent cut, the organization would “by necessity re-examine [its] position in Miami Beach.”

The city’s commissioners, including mayor Steven Meiner, voted 6 to 1 to push through a new contract with a rent of just $500,000 when the contract renewed in December 2026. The new deal also includes additional credits for fire, police, and EMT services from the city, which bring the annual savings up to $650,000, reports the Times . Other terms include a 30-day blackout period before and after Art Basel Miami Beach , during which other art fairs may not rent the convention center. Art Basel can also veto events in public parks or on the beach that take place in an “Art Basel zone” stretching about a square mile around the building.

A key conversation took place, according to the Times , at the home of Norman Braman, a Miami auto dealer and billionaire philanthropist who appeared on the ARTnews Top 200 Collectors list from 2003 to 2014. His was a central voice in persuading the fair to open in Miami Beach in the first place. Andrea Zappia, chief executive of MCH Group , Art Basel’s parent company, warned him of the possible relocation at the meeting at his home in December 2025, says the Times .

blocks.text: Braman called the demand of a rent reduction “offensive,” and called the threat to move a mere bluff. During a televised discussion on the renewal, notes the Times , Suarez called Braman and held his phone up to his microphone. Braman argued that the city should get better terms, pointing out that media titan James Murdoch invested about $80 million in the fair in 2020 and that the fair reported profits of almost $22 million in the first half of 2026, of which a large portion came from the Basel fairs. “It’s not up to taxpayers to subsidize private enterprise,” Braman told the meeting.

What’s more, Braman told the assembly, the Frieze art fair would move in to the convention center “in a moment’s notice.” A spokesperson for Frieze’s parent company, MARI, told the paper that claim was “completely untrue.”

For his part, Horowitz pleaded poverty, telling the meeting that Murdoch’s investment had been necessary to “stabilize” a company that had nearly faced insolvency, and that the fairs are currently facing “a cyclical downturn the likes of which we haven’t seen since the launch of Art Basel Miami Beach in the early 2000s.” He noted that the fair has shrunk from 283 exhibitors last year to just 250 expected this December.
